title: Around the World through Japan
summary: Walter Del Mar went round the world from west to east in 1898–99, and more than half of this book is about Japan. He sails from London by Marseilles and Suez to Ceylon, and goes on to Java, Singapore, Hong Kong, Canton, Macao, and Shanghai. In Japan he travels widely: Tokyo and Kyoto, Nara, the island of Shikoku and the Inland Sea, Kyushu and Satsuma, the main island from Tokuyama to Nagoya, Hakone, Hokkaido and the Ainu, Nikko and Asama-yama. Chapters follow on Japanese religion, entertainments, women, arts, and trade, and his impressions of the country. He returns by Hawaii, California, and the Yosemite valley, and across the United States by Colorado. The last chapter gives advice to tourists on routes, costs, and luggage. There are fifty plates of photographs.
